When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian **100** STRONG BUY (capitulation) vs Regime state **50** TRANSITION with RISK OFF bias and macro regime CONTRACTION at **70%**
One gauge says sellers are exhausted, the other says the economy is weakening. Trust the regime for sizing, since a contrarian buy signal can fire for weeks before a low forms. Use the contrarian reading only to stage small entries.
⚠ These two disagree: VIX Spike backwardation inactive (Tier **1** of **4**, BROAD) vs Confluence T1 x HYG and T1 x JPY both ACTIVE, and both are built on VIX backwardation
The confluence labels assume a stressed VIX curve while the spike detector says the curve is not inverted. Trust the spike detector for the curve itself. Treat the two confluences as early warning from credit and yen, not as proof that options markets are panicking.
⚠ These two disagree: Divergence composite net bias **-12** vs **16** bullish pairs against only **4** bearish pairs out of **43**
Most diverging pairs lean bullish, yet the weighted net bias is negative. The heavily weighted pairs (yield curve, bond volatility, chips, regional banks) carry the bearish load. Trust the weighted read, because those pairs matter more for risk.

AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The tape is breaking in the US while the rest of the world holds. The Nasdaq 100 is down 9.4% over five days and the Dow is down only 1.6%, so the damage sits in growth and tech. The Crash Index reads 4/10, which puts it in WARNING with three or more signals live. The regime model calls CONTRACTION at 70% confidence.

The contrarian score at 100 says investors have capitulated, and that part is true. It does not say the low is in. With 4 risk off signals aligned and a TRANSITION score of 50, you should hold smaller size than the contrarian screen suggests. Stage any buying in small pieces, and keep the core book lighter until credit and yen stop flashing. Two confluences are active (2 of 3), both tied to credit stress and yen safe haven flow.

The main risk is a VIX curve that inverts from here. Today backwardation is off and the spike detector sits at Tier 1 of 4 with a 50% probability. A flip to backwardation, with high yield credit still weak, would turn this from a fast correction into a funding story. If the VIX curve stays normal and the Crash Index drops back under 3, the contrarian buy starts to work.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The regime model reads CONTRACTION at 70% confidence, and the regime state score of 50 (TRANSITION) says the shift is not finished. Contraction usually favors cash flow, short duration quality and defensive sectors over long duration growth. That fits the Nasdaq 100 drop of 9.4%.

Position for slower growth. Hold more cash than your normal book, rotate toward balance sheet strength, and keep rate sensitive bets small because stocks and long bonds have stopped moving together (spy_tlt_corr60 at -0.15). The contrarian score of 100 gives you a reason to build a watchlist, not to rebuild a full position. A confidence reading falling below 50%, or the regime moving out of CONTRACTION, would be the signal to add risk.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence here means two assets that normally move together have stopped doing so. Correlation drift is the measure: it compares how tightly a pair moved over a long window against how it moves now. The composite sits in the ELEVATED zone, with 46.5% of the 43 pairs diverging. The mother jaws score is 100. Net bias is -12, with 4 bearish and 16 bullish pairs.

Six pairs score 80 (DEEP DIVERG). The yield curve spread (t10y2y) moved from -0.51 to +0.29, so the relationship has flipped sign. Chips against the S&P (smh_spy) fell from +0.89 to -0.05: semiconductors no longer follow the index. Stocks against long bonds (spy_tlt_corr60) went from +0.76 to -0.15, which weakens bonds as a hedge. Regional banks against financials (kre_xlf) moved from +0.43 to -0.59, a sign of stress inside the banking group. Bond volatility (move) and ether against bitcoin (eth_btc) also flipped. When this many links break together, old hedges and pair trades stop working, so cut size on relative value positions and check what your hedges actually track.

Confluences — most proven alpha of the framework 2/3 ACTIVE
AI read · what the confluences mean now

Two of three confluence signals are active. The first is T1 x HYG, which pairs a rising VIX fear signal with credit stress in high yield bonds. The second is T1 x JPY, which pairs it with money running to the yen. Credit and yen are the two places where real stress shows up first, because lenders and carry traders move before equity buyers do. The small cap drawdown link (T1 x B2) is off, so the damage has not spread to the Russell yet.

Lean defensive on the way in. Keep new longs small, favor quality balance sheets over leveraged ones, and avoid adding to credit sensitive positions. Watch the third signal. If small caps join, the stress has moved from tech to the whole economy, and you should cut gross exposure further.

Asia · Europe · US · Crypto 24/7 — lead-lag detection
Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Asia and Europe are bouncing while the US sells off. In Asia, the Hang Seng leads at +3.6% over five days and the KOSPI lags at -15.5%. That Korean drop is severe, and with chips breaking from the S&P in the divergence data it fits a shock hitting the semiconductor chain. In Europe, the CAC leads at +3.7% and the FTSE lags at +1.3%, so every European index is positive.

The US is the weak link. The Dow leads at -1.6% and the Nasdaq 100 lags at -9.4%, a gap of nearly eight points that shows the pain is concentrated in growth. Crypto is mixed, with ether at -0.7% and Solana at -5.7%. The lead lag read for today's session: Europe and Hong Kong are holding up, so global money is not leaving risk assets in general. It is leaving US tech. Expect the US open to follow chips and Korea, and treat any bounce in the Nasdaq 100 without a stabilizing KOSPI as weak.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 4/10 · WARNING — 3+ signals, active surveillance
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

These two gauges agree more than they first appear to. The Crash Index scores 4/10, which means four of ten warning conditions in price and breadth are on. The VIX Spike Detector sits at Tier 1 of 4 (BROAD) with a 50% probability of a volatility jump, and skew is active. Skew means investors pay up for downside protection, which shows fear in options before it shows in the VIX itself.

Backwardation is off and the adaptive trigger is off. That keeps the options market in watchful mode rather than panic. Price damage is real (the Nasdaq 100 is down 9.4% in five days), but the cost of hedging has not exploded. That gap is where you want to look. If you hold tech risk, buy protection while skew is only active and the curve is normal, because it gets expensive fast once the curve inverts. A Crash Index of 6 or a move to Tier 2 would flip this to full defense.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 4/10 — a few early signals are stirring; watch whether more line up.

The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
